name: Geller Voiding Trial
question: How do retrograde-fill and spontaneous voiding trials compare in detecting prolonged postoperative voiding dysfunction after female pelvic floor surgery?

design.blinding: Patients and staff performing voiding trials were not blinded
design.population: 50 women undergoing surgery for urinary incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse, or both between November 2009 and March 2010.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 638; Figure 1, p 639

verdictNote: Retrograde testing was more specific; no prespecified between-method accuracy threshold was tested.
takeaway: In 50 women receiving both postoperative tests, retrograde-fill voiding trials had 94.4% sensitivity and 58.1% specificity for retention lasting more than 7 days, versus 100% and 25.8% with spontaneous trials; failure rates were 31/50 versus 42/50 (P=.001).

reports.label: Randomized-order diagnostic report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed and Crossref list September 2011, without a day
reports.citation: Geller EJ, Hankins KJ, Parnell BA, et al. "Diagnostic accuracy of retrograde and spontaneous voiding trials for postoperative voiding dysfunction: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(3):637-642. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318229e8dd
reports.followUp: Retention lasting more than 7 days was the diagnostic reference outcome; duration follow-up was available for 49/50 women
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, p 639; Results, p 640; Discussion, p 642

results.measure: Sensitivity and specificity (95% CI) for retention lasting more than 7 days; duration follow-up 49/50
results.note: Counts derive from Table 2 percentages and 49/50 duration follow-up; the paper did not prespecify a between-method accuracy threshold. Table 2 Fisher exact P values (<.001 retrograde; .02 spontaneous) assess association within each method, not between-method accuracy.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 640; Methods, p 639; Discussion, p 642

results.measure: Failure rate for each test across the paired cohort (P=.001)
results.note: Each woman underwent both tests; these are paired test-level rates, not randomized-sequence group rates. Counts derive from the reported percentages of 50.

results.measure: Positive and negative predictive values (95% CI) for retention lasting more than 7 days
results.note: Counts derive from Table 2 percentages and 49/50 duration follow-up; the paper does not print the two-by-two counts.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 640; Discussion, p 642

results.measure: Preferred voiding trial, irrespective of test order
results.note: The nonvalidated preference questionnaire has no printed denominator; order did not affect preference (P=.40), and the difference was not statistically significant.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 641; Discussion, p 642

results.measure: High postvoid residual or inadequate voided volume among 50 paired tests

values.spontaneous: 34/50 (68%) high postvoid residual; 8/50 (16%) inadequate voided volume

results.note: Counts derive from percentages of 50; all retrograde failures resulted from high postvoid residual.

harms.label: Duration of postoperative retention by paired-test failure pattern
harms.note: Women failing both tests had 12.6 ± 14.4 days of retention versus 2.5 ± 2.1 days among those failing only one test (P=.004); pattern-specific duration denominators were not printed; 49/50 had duration follow-up.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 639; Discussion, p 642

harms.label: Postoperative urinary tract infection
harms.note: P=.79; numerators and denominators for these postoperative UTI rates were not printed. Among those discharged self-catheterizing versus others, UTI occurred in 13.8% versus 17.6% (P=.99).

harms.label: Other postoperative complications

values.spontaneous: 1 postoperative transfusion and 1 postoperative fever in spontaneous-first sequence

harms.note: The paper reports no Clavien-Dindo grades for these events.

delivery.label: Paired testing and randomized order
delivery.value: All 50 women received both methods; 25 were randomized to retrograde first and 25 to spontaneous first.
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 1, p 639; Methods, p 638

delivery.label: Voiding trial protocol
delivery.value: On postoperative day 1, retrograde testing instilled 300 mL saline through the Foley catheter, then required a void within 30 minutes; residual was estimated by subtracting voided volume from 300 mL. Spontaneous testing allowed filling for up to 4 hours and required two consecutive passes. Postvoid residual >100 mL failed either method; spontaneous voided volume <200 mL was inadequate and counted as failure.

delivery.label: Management after failed test
delivery.value: Women failing either method were discharged on intermittent self-catheterization until two consecutive postvoid residuals <100 mL; no prophylactic antibiotics were given.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 638–639; Results, p 640
